content.user_title: Optimize Application Performance Across the Stack
content.value_statement: Teams need clear evidence before changing performance-critical systems. This skill guides profiling, optimization, testing, and monitoring across backend, frontend, and infrastructure.
actual_capabilities: Establishes performance baselines with profiling, tracing, real-user data, and critical journey metrics.
Coordinates database, backend, API, and distributed system optimization steps.
Guides frontend bundle, CDN, edge, mobile, and progressive web app optimization.
Designs load tests, stress tests, and automated performance regression checks.
Defines production monitoring, dashboards, SLOs, alerts, and continuous optimization routines.
limitations: Requires metrics, traces, profiles, or test data for accurate recommendations.
Does not run load tests or change infrastructure by itself.
Production testing still needs explicit approval, safeguards, and rollback plans.
Subagent names and tools must exist in the user's AI environment.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Slow User Journeys
use_cases.description: Map latency, rendering, database, and API bottlenecks before choosing fixes.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Traffic Growth
use_cases.description: Create capacity plans, load tests, and scaling targets for expected demand.

use_cases.title: Prevent Performance Regressions
use_cases.description: Add performance budgets, CI checks, dashboards, and alert rules for critical paths.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Baseline Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan performance profiling for my web app. Focus on response times, Core Web Vitals, and key user journeys.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Slow Service
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to analyze these profiling results and propose backend, database, and caching optimizations with measurable targets.

prompt_templates.title: Validate at Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design load tests for peak traffic, define success metrics, and create regression checks for CI.

prompt_templates.title: Build Continuous Optimization
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a full performance program with SLOs, dashboards, capacity planning, and a prioritized optimization backlog.

output_examples.input: Optimize checkout latency after recent traffic growth.
output: Baseline checkout P50, P95, P99, and error rates.
Profile database queries, API calls, cache misses, and frontend rendering.
Prioritize fixes by user impact, rollout risk, and measurable latency reduction.

output_examples.input: Create a performance regression plan for release pipelines.
output: Define performance budgets for key pages and endpoints.
Add load, API, and Lighthouse checks to CI.
Create rollback triggers for high latency, error spikes, or budget failures.

best_practices: Start with baseline metrics before choosing optimizations.
Run load tests only with approval, realistic scenarios, and rollback plans.
Connect every change to a measurable user or business metric.
anti_patterns: Optimizing isolated code paths without current profiling data.
Load testing production systems without explicit approval and safeguards.
Scaling infrastructure before reviewing known application and database bottlenecks.

faq.question: What systems does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers backend, frontend, database, CDN, mobile, observability, and load testing workflows.

faq.question: Can it run load tests for me?
faq.answer: No. It helps design and validate load tests. Operators must run approved tools in their environment.

faq.question: Does it require production access?
faq.answer: No. It can use staging and exported metrics. Production testing needs approval and safeguards.

faq.question: Which AI tools are supported?
faq.answer: It is structured for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with frontend performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes page load, interactivity, layout stability, bundle size, and mobile performance guidance.

faq.question: Will it guarantee lower costs?
faq.answer: No. It helps find cost and capacity options. Results depend on implementation, traffic, and workload behavior.
